title: EPF reports income growth eases in 3Q, warns slowdown may persist in 4Q
text:
EPF reports income growth eases in 3Q, warns slowdown may persist in 4Q Tuesday 17 Nov 2026 BURSA SGX Home 
 Highlight Make The Edge Malaysia your preferred source on Google KUALA LUMPUR (Nov 16): The Employees Provident Fund (EPF) reported that its investment income growth decelerated in the third quarter and warned that the slowdown could persist.
 Investment income grew just 3% in the third quarter from a year earlier, the fund also known by the EPF said in a statement, compared to a blistering 44% year-on-year gain in the second quarter. The trend could continue in the final quarter amid global equities downturn and rising bond yields, it said. 
 Risks around government borrowing, continued inflation and the valuation of stocks related to artificial intelligence (AI) have become elevated at the start of this quarter, said chief executive Ahmad Zulqarnain Onn.
 “These developments require us to be disciplined in managing the portfolio, balancing opportunities against emerging risks while remaining focused on sustainable long-term returns and the retirement security of our members,” he added.
 Investment income for the three months ended Sept 30 amounted to RM25.82 billion. Equities accounted for over two-thirds of total investment income, generating RM17.41 billion in income for the one of the world’s largest pension funds.
 Growth was supported by corporate earnings, continued investment in AI-related sectors and generally favourable economic conditions.
 Fixed-income contributed RM7.12 billion, or 28% of the investment income, despite valuation pressures arising from higher bond yields across major markets. Real estate and infrastructure investments generated RM890 million, while money market instruments contributed RM400 million.
 International investments, which represented 38% of total investment assets, generated RM13.68 billion, accounting for 53% of the fund's investment income during the quarter.
 Of the RM25.82 billion earned during the quarter, RM21.39 billion was attributable to Simpanan Konvensional and RM4.43 billion to Simpanan Shariah.
 Investment income in the first nine months totalled RM83.32 billion, a 30% increase when compared to the same period last year.
 At the end of September, total assets stood at RM1.55 trillion, with equities making up 47.1% of the portfolio, followed by fixed income at 44%, real estate and infrastructure at 5.6%, and money market instruments at 3.3%.
 EPF membership
 The EPF also reported a 13% increase in total membership to 18.67 million as at September.
 Active membership grew 23.8% to 11.23 million from 9.07 million, bringing the ratio of active to inactive members to 60:40.
 However, new registrations fell nearly 70% to 658,777 members from 2.17 million in the corresponding period last year.
 The number of active employers, meanwhile, increased 2.9% to 646,686 firms, although new employer registrations declined 12.9% to 54,336.
